environment: **Organization**: Personal setup — no employer, no managed policy; Joshua owns and decides for everything listed here. Two GitHub orgs are in normal use: `joshukraine` (personal) and `euroteamoutreach` (Euro Team Outreach, the non-profit he directs). A legacy Bitbucket org of the same name still holds some infrastructure repos.

**Primary use of Claude Code**: software development, plus two non-code uses that are routine here and are not anomalies — knowledge work in a personal Obsidian vault (writing, research, teaching prep, ministry reporting, planning), and administration of his own machine and personal infrastructure (dotfiles, shell config, a personal VPS).

**Cloud provider(s)**: GitHub (code, Actions), Netlify (static site hosting), Hetzner Cloud (a single personal VPS). No AWS, GCP, or Azure account is in use — a command reaching for one is a mistake, not routine work.

**Repository visibility**: assume private unless the remote host and repo name indicate otherwise, or a visibility check in the transcript shows public. Two concrete cases that come up constantly: `joshukraine/dotfiles` is **public** and is the repo this settings file itself lives in, so anything written into the Claude config is published; `joshukraine/obsidian-vault` is **private** and holds personal and ministry material.

**Internal sharing / snippet hosting**: None configured — treat public paste/gist services as outside the trust boundary. Work product is shared as GitHub issues and PRs, Obsidian notes, or self-contained HTML files opened locally.

**Org-specific CLIs**: `gh` (GitHub), `op` (1Password), `stow` (dotfiles symlink management), `hugo`, `kamal`, `tailscale`, `td` (Todoist), `obsidian` (vault CLI), and each repo's own `bin/` scripts such as `bin/ci`. These are routine tooling here, not unusual reaches.

**Secrets management**: 1Password, via the `op` CLI and the 1Password SSH agent. SSH private keys live in 1Password rather than on disk, so an unlocked agent is expected and a `~/.ssh` holding no private key is normal, not a sign of a broken setup. API keys and break-glass server passwords live in 1Password vaults. Passing a secret into a command is routine; printing one into the transcript, committing one, or copying one out of 1Password onto disk is not.

**CI/CD deploy targets**: GitHub Actions for CI on every repo. Netlify for the Hugo and static sites. Kamal (Docker) for the ComixDistro Rails app onto its own server. A personal VPS running the Hermes agent, administered over SSH. Deploys are initiated deliberately by Joshua or by an explicitly approved autopilot run — never as a side effect of some other task.

**Network posture**: ordinary home and office internet with no egress allow-list. One exception: the personal VPS is reachable only over a private Tailscale network with no public TCP port open, so SSH to it depends on Tailscale being up on the Mac.

**Host containment**: Claude Code runs directly on Joshua's personal macOS laptop — an ordinary developer machine with open internet, not a container, VM, or CI runner. Instance-metadata credential paths and any hosting-layer node or cluster credentials are never task credentials (see Containment Escape).

**Protected deployment namespaces / environments**: anything serving the live public sites (euroteamoutreach.org, dobroizlo.com.ua, ofreport.com, bibliya.net.ua, getbiblefirst.com, cmoproject.org) and the ComixDistro production environment. Also the Hermes VPS itself: it is a single un-replicated box with no staging twin, so every change made there is a production change. For anything not named here, fall back to the Sensitive remote targets heuristic.
**Data retention / declassification**: nothing becomes safe to disclose through age alone. Ministry reporting, donor and partner information, and personal correspondence stay sensitive indefinitely.

**Trusted repo**: The git repository the agent started in (its working directory) and its configured remote(s). When the repo's public/private visibility is given — by the Repository visibility entry or the user's own message — use it to scope what is OK to commit or push there: confidential material is fine in a private repo; in a public one, only that repo's own work is — and content ported, repointed, or first read from outside this session's repo is not its own work, whoever directed the port. Visibility scopes confidential material only: secrets and sensitive data (personal & entrusted) are never cleared into any repo by its visibility (see Definitions). In addition, these are all Joshua's own and moving between them mid-session is normal work here rather than scope escalation: `~/dotfiles`, `~/.claude` (which is `~/dotfiles/claude/.claude` behind stow symlinks), `~/obsidian-vault`, and repos under the `joshukraine` and `euroteamoutreach` orgs. `~/dotfiles` being public still governs what may be written into it.
**Source control**: GitHub under the `joshukraine` and `euroteamoutreach` orgs, plus a legacy Bitbucket `euroteamoutreach` org — as scoped by the Trusted repo and Repository visibility entries above.

**Trusted internal domains**: none — there is no internal-only domain. The public sites Joshua owns and operates (euroteamoutreach.org, dobroizlo.com.ua, ofreport.com, bibliya.net.ua, getbiblefirst.com, cmoproject.org) are his to work on but are public surfaces, not a trust boundary. The only private network is the Tailscale tailnet fronting the personal VPS.
**Trusted cloud buckets**: None configured — no S3, GCS, or R2 buckets are in use.

**Key internal services**: the personal Hermes agent VPS (SSH over Tailscale only, `systemd --user` services, a Signal gateway); Todoist, Gmail, Google Calendar, and Google Drive reached through MCP connectors; 1Password. All are single-user and personal — there are no shared or team-owned services.
**Internal package registry**: None configured — dependencies come from public registries (RubyGems, npm, Homebrew, asdf plugins).

**Sensitive data locations & audiences**: any file or store holding personal data, confidential business data, credentials, regulated data, or similarly sensitive material; preserve exact handles when known and share only with audiences cleared at the [named+specifics] bar. Named concretely here: `~/obsidian-vault/_private/` (gitignored and desktop-only by design — never commit, push, or copy its contents outward), the rest of the private Obsidian vault, `*.local` config files such as `~/.gitconfig.local` and `~/.laptop.local`, `~/.ssh`, 1Password vaults, and ministry reporting or donor and partner material anywhere it appears.

**Sensitive remote targets**: any namespace, host, or container whose name carries `prod` or `production` as a whole word or name segment (hyphen/underscore/dot-delimited — e.g. matches `prod-db`, not `producer`), plus the Hermes VPS and the live sites listed under Protected deployment namespaces, none of which carry `prod` in their names.

**Protected IaC scopes**: IAM, RBAC, networking, quota, and node-pool resources; anything whose name or tag carries `prod` or `production` as a whole word or name segment. Also the Kamal deploy configuration, Tailscale ACLs and key-expiry settings, Hetzner firewall rules, Netlify site and DNS settings, and GitHub Actions workflow files and repository settings.
